evals.name: default-fire-and-forget-single
evals.prompt: Use orchestrate-using-herdr for the agreed cache-key validation fix. We are in the repository root checkout. We already agreed to validate keys in the save path and reuse the existing KeyError type. No flags.
evals.expected_output: Writes a to-spec-shaped spec into the brief (no ticket), carries the agreed save-path and KeyError details as binding, creates a worktree from the parent source with --no-focus, starts a pi worker, dispatches one brief ending with ulw, confirms acceptance, reports the handoff, and stops.
expectations: Creates no issue-tracker ticket without --track.
Marks the agreed implementation details binding in the brief.
Stops after confirmed prompt acceptance without monitoring.

evals.name: linked-worktree-uses-parent-source
evals.prompt: Use orchestrate-using-herdr for the agreed parser repair. The current cwd is a linked worktree at /repos/app/.worktrees/fix-parser; `herdr worktree list` reports source_checkout_path=/repos/app.
evals.expected_output: Creates the new worktree from /repos/app, not from the linked-worktree cwd.
expectations: Uses herdr worktree list before creation and parses the parent source.
Stops before creation if no parent source resolves.

evals.name: track-reuses-ticket-and-supervises
evals.prompt: Use orchestrate-using-herdr --track with existing Linear issue ENG-42 at https://linear.app/acme/issue/ENG-42 for the import validation repair.
evals.expected_output: Reuses ENG-42 unchanged, names the worktree and agent eng-42-<slug>, sends the ticket link plus context the ticket lacks, supervises the worker to a verified result checked at the destination, and comments the result on ENG-42.
expectations: Does not create or rewrite the supplied ticket.
Does not treat Herdr done as success without destination evidence.
Closes out on the ticket in Markdown.

evals.name: batch-needs-confirmed-plan
evals.prompt: Use orchestrate-using-herdr to review Jira issues OPS-41, OPS-42 and OPS-43 with the same rollout-risk rubric. I haven't decided whether I want ticket feedback or reviews of the linked code.
evals.expected_output: Stops before dispatch, clarifies ticket feedback versus linked-code review, proposes a per-item plan (targets, side effects, evidence, worker kind, concurrency, isolation, lifecycle), and waits for explicit confirmation.
expectations: Does not dispatch before explicit plan confirmation.
Writes no per-item spec; uses one shared instruction.

evals.name: auto-merge-fails-closed
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr --auto. The worker reported PR #12 at head abc123. Required checks are green, but the configured AI reviewer has not responded to abc123 after the worker's last push. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: Leaves PR #12 open with evidence because the reviewer gate for the current head is not closed; does not merge or bypass protection; reports the exact blocker.
expectations: Re-checks the head SHA before any merge.
Treats a silent reviewer as an open gate, not approval.

evals.name: watch-authorizes-local-dependency-checkpoints
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr --watch for three agreed implementation tickets. Tickets B and C depend on A. Mode and Git-skill defaults require explicit commit permission. No push, PR, or merge was requested. State the Git authority and relevant brief clauses; do not run commands.
evals.expected_output: Treats invocation as explicit authorization for scoped local implementation commits and dependency checkpoints. Includes that permission in worker briefs and does not ask separately for commit approval. Preserves normal hooks and unrelated work; does not authorize push, PR, merge, deployment, or history rewriting and does not edit global instructions or mode prompts.
expectations: Allows local dependency checkpoints without another approval question.
Carries local-commit permission explicitly into implementation briefs.
Keeps publication, merge, deployment, and history rewriting outside this local permission.
Changes no global or mode authorization defaults.

evals.name: review-followup-stays-worker-owned
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: a pi worker finished the implementation and published PR #198. Now address its review comments and an existing failing test gate. Most implementation context is noise for this phase. One comment needs only a short reply. Explain routing without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Delegates the review-comment and test-gate workflow through the worker using Handoff for the new phase. The orchestrator checks returned evidence and destination state, returning missing evidence to the worker rather than performing repairs or posting the short reply itself.
expectations: Keeps execution with the pi worker rather than taking over small tasks.
Uses Handoff because the settled unit enters a new phase with mostly noisy context.
Retains orchestrator acceptance and verification without duplicating worker execution.

evals.name: explicit-no-commit-overrides-default
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr --watch for the agreed parser fix, but leave all work uncommitted. Explain worker authority without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Carries the explicit no-commit restriction into the worker brief, leaves changes uncommitted, and does not reinterpret the skill's default as permission to commit or publish.
expectations: Honors the explicit no-commit instruction.
Does not authorize commits, publication, or merge.

evals.name: dependent-implementation-uses-stack-bases
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: orchestrate-using-herdr --watch for three agreed changes: foundation, authorization, and execution. Authorization depends on foundation; execution depends on authorization. The agreed root base is main. Plan the implementation branch topology and worker briefs. No publication was requested; do not run commands.
evals.expected_output: Plans a gh stack rooted at main: the foundation implementation branch bases on main, authorization bases on foundation, and execution bases on authorization. Carries branch and prerequisite-base identities into worker briefs and maintains these dependencies throughout implementation without publishing PRs.
expectations: Uses gh stack for the dependent implementation branches, not three independent main-based branches.
Names the correct root and immediate prerequisite base for every layer in worker briefs.
Keeps publication and history rewriting outside the local implementation authority.

evals.name: publication-continues-implementation-stack
evals.prompt: Offline simulation: three workers completed and verified an existing gh stack in their worktrees: feature/foundation on main, feature/auth on feature/foundation, and feature/execution on feature/auth. The workers are idle and their worktrees clean. Publish these changes as three dependent PRs. Explain which branches and worktrees you use and how you preserve recovery points; do not run commands.
evals.expected_output: Routes authorized publication through the existing workers using the existing implementation branches and worktrees, with PR bases main, feature/foundation, and feature/auth respectively. Preserves recovery points with backup refs if needed rather than creating a second publication stack. Keeps merge and history-rewrite authorization separate.
expectations: Publishes from feature/foundation, feature/auth, and feature/execution in their existing worktrees with the correct chained PR bases.
Does not create replacement publication branches merely to preserve original worker branches as immutable.
Uses backup refs when recovery points are needed and retains worker execution ownership.
Does not infer merge or history-rewrite permission from publication permission.
